text:
alex chen: FYI starting a short project to unbundle routing from the orchestrator. Aim: smaller deploy surface for routing rules and faster iteration for traffic policies. RFC follow-up: need cutover plan, DB safety, and alert thresholds.

maria gonzalez: Good to know. Is this driven by scale issues or product velocity?

alex chen: Both. We've seen tail latency on heavy orchestration cycles and product teams want to push routing rules more frequently.

jamal roberts: DB collision risk is my top worry. Right now both orchestrator and routing touch tenant_routing table. Any plan to avoid prolonged dual-writes?

sasha li: Suggest a short "write-fence" technique: keep orchestrator authoritative until we run a sharded promotion that atomically moves a tenant to the new service. Minimizes dual-write window.

alex chen: Plan sketch: 1) deploy routing-service read-only, 2) mirror requests for 48h, 3) compare outputs with a diff job, 4) open canary cohort (10% tenants) with writes, 5) batch-shard promote remaining tenants in maintenance window, 6) deprecate orchestrator routing. Rollback: flip cohort back to orchestrator per tenant.

jamal roberts: For the compare job, I'll build a pipeline that computes a per-tenant diff histogram and signal if >0.05% mismatches in 1h. Who owns the runner?

maria gonzalez: I'll own perf baselines and thresholds. My suggestion: p95 latency no greater than current + 12%, error rate <0.3% during canary.

sasha li: Need to add sequence_number on routing events and an idempotency key for writes. That avoids reordering and duplicate application semantics. Contract change is tiny.

alex chen: Good. Also add trace-id passthrough so we can join traces between orchestrator and routing-service during shadowing. Observability list: traces, per-tenant QPS, diff-rate metric, latency histograms, promotion-heartbeat.

maria gonzalez: Add an automated alert: if diff_rate > 0.1% over 30m -> auto rollback and page oncall.

jamal roberts: DB migration detail: propose creating a promotion table that records tenant -> owner service mapping. Promotion is a single short txn that flips a tenant's owner. That avoids global locks. We'll need a small compatibility shim in orchestrator to consult the mapping.

sasha li: I'll implement the shim as a lightweight feature-flagged check. Also add e2e that replays 24h of production traffic to validate no state drift.

alex chen: Owners: jamal = diff pipeline & db migration plan, maria = perf + SLO signoff, sasha = contract tests & shims. I'll write the runbook and the rollback steps.

ops-bot: New task created: CORE-2021 routing-unbundle (owners: alex, jamal, maria, sasha).

maria gonzalez: Cost note: mirroring doubles hotpath ingress. We'll need a temporary infra budget and an ops queue for any spikes.

jamal roberts: During promotion window we should reserve an SRE on-call slot and a maintenance page for 60 minutes. If anything goes sideways we un-promote the last batch.

sasha li: Also add a debug endpoint that returns the last_applied_sequence for a tenant. Extremely helpful for quick checks.

alex chen: Agreed. We'll also tag a small group of "canary power users" who can be first responders if we see customer-facing issues.

maria gonzalez: Timeline proposal: Week A: infra + spec + tickets, Week B: shadow + compare, Week C: canary cohort, Week D: shard promotion + cleanup. Flexible for DB signoff.

jamal roberts: I'll open CORE-2021 with sub-tasks and owners. Please add any missing dependencies (eg. marketplace integrations).

sasha li: I'll add contract matrix and schedule the replay test.

alex chen: Let's sync tomorrow 9:30am PT for a 20m alignment: DB migration approach, cohort selection heuristics, observability thresholds, cost estimate. Bring blockers.

maria gonzalez: 44d I'll bring baseline numbers.

jamal roberts: 44d I'll bring the pipeline sketch.

sasha li: 44d I'll bring the contract checklist.

alex chen: Thanks. If anyone spots a hidden dependency (eg. third-party auth hook) call it out here before the sync.

ops-bot: CORE-2021 created and linked to sprint board.

alex chen: End of thread.
